# The Spiral Arms That Hold Us Close

## Scripture
*"He wraps himself in light as with a garment; he stretches out the heavens like a tent."* — Psalm 104:2

## Reflection
On clear October evenings, if you escape the city lights, you can trace the faint river of the Milky Way arching overhead. What our ancestors saw as spilled milk, we now know is a vast spiral galaxy—hundreds of billions of stars, including our own sun, slowly wheeling around a common center. We live inside that great turning, tucked between spiral arms, held in place by gravity we cannot see but cannot escape.

The psalmist didn't know about galaxies. He simply looked up and understood something true: the God who made all this is not distant from it. Like a tent stretched over travelers, the heavens are His handiwork—and He does not abandon what He makes. The same invisible force that keeps a galaxy from flying apart keeps His children. You are not drifting alone through autumn's darkening skies.

If God holds billions of stars in their patient orbit, He can hold your life too—your questions, your waiting, your small and hidden faithfulness. The spiral arms turn slowly, but they turn faithfully. So does His care for you.

Step outside tonight. Let the vastness remind you: the Maker of galaxies knows your name, and His grip is gentler and stronger than gravity itself.

## Prayer
Lord of the heavens, You stretch out the stars and hold them in their courses. When I feel small beneath the autumn sky, remind me that You who keep galaxies in orbit also keep me. Wrap me in Your light, steady my wandering heart, and let me rest in the gravity of Your love. Amen.
